entries.test: Public proof records and accounts of its development would establish whether humans contributed to the claimed solution.
entries.note: Marcus explicitly rejects the claim that AI solved it alone.
This concerns what AI could have accomplished in an alternative process without human help; the actual collaboration cannot settle that counterfactual.

entries.test: Public development logs, proof materials, and participant accounts would establish the extent of Alpöge's guidance in producing the claimed proof.
entries.note: The plain reading concerns human involvement in the actual process.
No shared criterion specifies when this result would establish AGI or why human guidance would exclude it.

entries.test: The public proof's page count and mathematical literature available at publication would establish its length and whether general lessons, techniques, or concepts had been introduced.
entries.note: The proposition drops the knowledge hedge on new techniques and concepts. Its factual core is checkable, although elegance is subjective.

entries.test: Public proof documentation and inventories of medical formal-verification resources would establish reliance on Lean and mathlib and the availability of comparable resources in medicine.
entries.note: The following sentences identify the resources as Lean and mathlib.
“Presumably” makes this a qualified assessment. Dropping “relatively” also strengthens the proposition.

entries.test: Public technical documentation and comparative studies would establish how formal verification works in mathematics and what obstacles arise when applying it in other domains.
entries.note: This has a plain technical reading about formally specifying and verifying correctness.

entries.test: Public evaluations of gains from verifiable AI methods across domains, together with Marcus's 2024 publications, would test the comparative claim and the claimed earlier prediction.
entries.note: The comparison is broad but makes an empirical claim about demonstrated benefits.
Neither the hoped-for generality nor what would make it obvious is specified. He does not firmly assert that the methods cannot generalize.
The source offers a tentative personal analogy, while the proposition states the resemblance firmly. The analogy supplies no shared test for how closely the two achievements resemble each other.

entries.test: Public listing records and after-hours trading data around the announcement would establish whether Anthropic stock traded and whether its price moved materially.
entries.note: The existence of the asserted trading market is itself publicly checkable.

entries.test: Public reliability evaluations, documented failures, and application-specific performance requirements would show whether current AI falls short in many applications.
entries.note: The plain reading concerns practical reliability for deployment.
Profitability and investment amounts are factual, but whether those investments are warranted is an investment-value judgment without a stated decision rule.
